title: ThreatDown ransomware detections
volume: None on a normal day. Each blocked ransomware process makes one detection, in the endpoint's case.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: One custom detection rule for ThreatDown Nebula and OneView, on the Antivirus records the library's ThreatDown parsers write from its syslog. It makes a detection when ThreatDown's ransomware protection blocks a process. It matches sensor type ThreatDown only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's ThreatDown parsers, and turn on Syslog Logging in Nebula or OneView to the data collector, as the parser entry says. Then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.

How it works:
- The parsers write ThreatDown's ransomware category (arw) as the threat category RANSOMWARE, with the process and the endpoint.
- Malware, PUP and PUM detections go to the same schema and aren't taken: ThreatDown quarantines those itself.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 3 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 28 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on any of the samples, the Antivirus records included.
- The lines went to HTTP Ingest one per request as text, the way a syslog line arrives.

Known gaps:
- The syslog endpoint polls the console and buffers up to 24 hours, so a detection can come well after the event.
